info.name: URL Shortener — Full Suite (Days 1-9)
info.description:
Cumulative end-to-end test suite for the URL shortener, Day 1 through Day 9. One collection that runs standalone from a clean DB and exercises every implemented surface:

  • Day 1-2  Health + Auth (register/login/refresh/logout, validation, no-enumeration)
  • Day 3    URL shortening (Base62, custom alias, ttl)
  • Day 4-5  Redirect 302 (cache-aside) on the redirect server
  • Day 6    Rate-limit headers
  • Day 7+9  Async analytics (clicks → worker → summary/events) + IDOR
  • Day 8    Input validation edge cases, helmet security headers, CORS allow-list

PREREQUISITES
  1. Run all three processes:  api (:3000),  redirect (:3001),  worker.
  2. Postman → Settings → 'Automatically follow redirects: OFF' (so 302s are visible).
  3. Clicks are processed ASYNC by the worker; the Analytics Summary request waits ~4s in a pre-request script. Under the collection runner add a per-request Delay of ~3000ms for safety.

This collection generates unique emails/aliases per run (Date.now()), so it is safe to re-run without manual cleanup.

item.name: 4. Shorten (Day 3 + Day 8 validation)
item.description: Note on rate limiting: POST /api/urls is limited to 10 creates / 60s PER USER (Day 6). Every attempt — even one that will fail validation — consumes a token, because the rate-limit preHandler runs before body validation. To keep the suite green on default config, the valid creates + the first batch of negative cases run as the PRIMARY user (10 total), and the remaining negative cases run as the SECOND user (Bearer {{second_access_token}}). Validation outcome is independent of which user is authenticated, so this is purely to stay under the per-user limit.

exec: pm.test('Status 400 — dangerous scheme rejected', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(400); });
